content.jointProblem: Can a Serbian-specific retrieval pipeline combining script canonicalization, morphological normalization and updateable vocabulary handling reduce LinguaBot’s no-useful-result rate from 18% toward its below-5% target without requiring full re-indexing? The first experiment would compare these components against the current Elasticsearch baseline on held-out support queries, explicitly testing transfer from document-retrieval research to short banking and telecom queries, including within-word script mixing, while measuring retrieval quality, latency and vocabulary-update effort.

rationale.text: His research directly examines how Serbian morphological reduction interacts with script normalization, providing a basis for testing pipeline ordering rather than treating these problems independently.

sources.quote: U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa.

rationale.text: He has evaluated phoneme-based canonicalization for Serbian cross-script retrieval, offering a concrete alternative to simple script conversion.

sources.quote: The phoneme-based canonical form reduced the out-of-vocabulary rate from 9.3% to 2.1% compared with a Latin-only baseline

rationale.text: His transliteration research explicitly addresses exceptions such as loanwords, abbreviations and alphanumeric strings, which merit targeted testing on company terminology.

sources.quote: Deterministic rule-based transliteration between Serbian Cyrillic and Latin scripts handles the majority of tokens correctly, but fails on foreign loanwords, abbreviations, and alphanumeric strings.

rationale.text: He has studied latency–accuracy trade-offs in script-normalizing retrieval, including selective neural fallback, supporting an experimentally grounded deployment choice.

sources.quote: A cascaded configuration — deterministic normalizer with neural fallback triggered only for out-of-vocabulary tokens — reaches MRR of 0.66 with a 99th-percentile latency overhead of only 9 ms.

rationale.text: His work includes search-framework integration in company pilots, although this does not establish compatibility with LinguaBot’s Elasticsearch configuration.

sources.quote: Administrativni troškovi uvođenja bili su niski jer je modul integrisan kao dodatak bez izmene ostatka sistema.

constraints.text: The solution must address Serbian-specific inflection and automatic script-mixing tolerance within the existing Elasticsearch search workflow, rather than fixing script variation alone.

sources.quote: Our current Elasticsearch setup uses a basic stemmer that was built for Croatian and misses a significant share of Serbian-specific forms.
our users freely switch between Latin and Cyrillic script mid-sentence — sometimes mid-word in typos.

constraints.text: New vocabulary must be accommodated without a full re-index, and maintenance cannot depend on continually expanding manual synonym lists.

sources.quote: can be updated when new vocabulary arrives without a full re-index.
maintaining those lists manually does not scale as clients add new product terminology every quarter.

constraints.text: Evaluation should use the available labelled query-response data and linguist validation; the below-5% miss rate is a target to test, not an established outcome.

sources.quote: We have a labelled query-response dataset of around 85,000 pairs across all clients, and our two in-house linguists can annotate or validate proposed solutions.
A good outcome is getting that 18% miss rate below 5% and keeping it there with a manageable maintenance process.

constraints.text: Tooling and data work must fit the approximately EUR 8,000 budget, with a testable prototype within six months.

sources.quote: Budget for tooling or data work is modest — around 8,000 EUR — and we want something testable within six months.

constraints.text: The researcher's contribution must be scoped as a small industrial engagement because he is already committed to two active projects.

sources.quote: Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.

constraints.text: The engagement must retain a defined research question rather than becoming a general software-development assignment.

sources.quote: nije zainteresovan za opšte projekte razvoja softvera bez istraživačke komponente.

risks: Most cited methods were tested on legal, news, web or encyclopedia collections, not LinguaBot’s support traffic. Their effectiveness on short queries, product names and within-word mixed-script typos remains unvalidated and must be tested in the first experiment.

Incremental document indexing does not establish that changes to morphological or canonicalization rules can be applied without rebuilding existing index representations. The no-full-re-index requirement may limit feasible designs.
Prior company pilots required terminology updates, so reusing those approaches could reproduce the manual-maintenance burden the company wants to eliminate.
The reported error attribution covers more than half of misses, not all misses. Fixing morphology and script confusion alone may therefore be insufficient to reach a miss rate below 5%.
Participation in joint projects is open, but the researcher's start date and weekly availability remain unknown despite the stated capacity for a small engagement.
Data-access permissions, privacy requirements, deployment hardware, latency limits and the coverage of research or integration costs beyond the tooling/data budget are unknown.
questions: What start date, weekly commitment and deliverables can the researcher support within a small six-month joint project, and who will own production integration?
Can the researcher access anonymized queries, target knowledge-base documents and relevance labels across clients, and what client approvals or data-location restrictions apply?
How is 'no useful result' defined, at what retrieval depth is it measured, and can the 12,000-query bank baseline be reproduced using a temporally held-out evaluation set?

Which Elasticsearch version, analyzers and index mappings are deployed, and does 'without a full re-index' permit an initial migration or auxiliary index while requiring subsequent vocabulary changes to be incremental?
What are the production latency, throughput, memory and hardware limits, and are external APIs or neural components permitted?
Does EUR 8,000 cover only tooling and data work, or also researcher fees and integration; how much time can the four ML engineers and two linguists commit?

Which new-term and within-word script-mixing examples should form the first stress test, and what limits on precision loss and maintenance effort will determine whether a candidate pipeline is acceptable?
